extra_findings: F3 — listing/search shows every client's tickets (index.php:72-74, lib.php:78-93): visibility rule not enforced on the listing; fixed with listarChamadosVisiveis
F4 — CSV export returns every ticket to any logged-in client (index.php:44-47, lib.php:132); fixed by filtering the web export to the client's tickets while exportarCsv() still returns all
F8 (secondary part) — export written to a fixed shared on-disk file EXPORT_DIR/chamados.csv left with all tickets (lib.php:125-150)
F12 — N+1 in the CSV export (lib.php:137); same root as PERF-001, attributed once
F13 — no brute-force / rate limiting on login (index.php:21-29); not fixed
F15 — visibility rule absent from the data layer (ARCH-003-like), mitigated with *Visiveis() variants
F16 — array GET/POST parameters (login[], busca[]) cause TypeError/500 (index.php:22, 72)
F17 — fputcsv without $escape: deprecated in PHP 8.4 and non-RFC-4180 backslash escaping (lib.php:130, 138)
F18 — connect_errno check dead under PHP >= 8.1; uncaught mysqli_sql_exception leaks user/host (index.php:9-13)
F19 — mediaResposta loads all rows into PHP to average (lib.php:109-115)
F21 — integer concatenated into SQL in tecnicoNome/verChamado (lib.php:69, 100); report correctly states it is not exploitable today (hardening)
F22 — PERF-002: SELECT * without pagination, including TEXT column (lib.php:80); not fixed
notes: achados.json binding (LEB-100-A, 1.1, matrix sha 68088ab…) matches the delivered package. JSON and prose are consistent (22 findings, same ids). No decoy reported: F22 mentions that LIKE '%x%' does not use an index but proposes no index (not PERF-006). Judgment calls: (1) BUG-004 credited via F8, whose mechanism explicitly cites the unclosed $fp on query failure at lines 133-135, filed under 'seguranca' -> C1 half. (2) ARCH-002 credited R1 full only via the Decisions list of deliberate non-changes. (3) exportarCsv no longer writes EXPORT_DIR/chamados.csv; the manifest only contracts 'escreve o CSV na saída', so not COMP, and the report flags it as a deploy checklist item. (4) The web export is filtered to the client's own tickets while exportarCsv() without a session still returns all tickets: enforcement, not COMP-003. (5) fputcsv with escape '' changes bytes only for backslash+quote values; header text/order and Status labels preserved; characterization 22/22 green. (6) listarChamados adds an id DESC tiebreak to ORDER BY criado_em DESC and normalizes values back to strings: same contract. (7) Connection failure now returns HTTP 500 instead of 200 with the same message; not a contracted route effect. (8) SEC-001 leaves % and _ unescaped by deliberate choice; C3 is probe-driven (full).

expl_justification.clareza: It has a Resumo with counts (22 findings, 19 fixed), a numbered pre-deploy checklist that includes rollback, uniform Onde/Categoria-severidade-confianca/Mecanismo/Impacto/O que fiz/Evidencia blocks, a Decisoes list, a section of consciously assumed trade-offs with how to undo each, and a verification table with honest limits. It is organized and direct.
expl_justification.precisao: The claims are accurate and deep: the 9-column UNION puts senha in the Titulo position; mysqli::query rules out stacked statements; PHP 7 gave NAN where PHP 8 throws; a naive UPDATE in CHAR(32) under a permissive sql_mode silently truncates the bcrypt, hence the guard; prepared statements return ints, hence 'linhaComoTexto'; SUM/COUNT keeps 25.666666666666668; the 8.4 deprecation fires before header(); an empty escape changes bytes only for data containing a backslash before a quote; and the export race is honestly reported as not reproduced, at confidence 80. One slip: F1 says the payload makes the grid show 'login e hash', but in that row login lands in descricao, which the listing does not render.
expl_justification.causa_raiz: Every finding gives a concrete, mostly reproduced path, and F15 names the structural cause: the public readers cannot know the user, so 'as tres rotas de leitura ... esqueceram (F2, F3, F4). Qualquer rota futura repetira o erro', mitigated by variants that require the scope with no default. It also explains why a shared file is harmless today but would leak once scoping exists.
expl_justification.priorizacao: The findings run strictly by severity (1 critica, 6 alta, 8 media, 7 baixa) with confidence. Confidence is lowered where evidence is weaker (F8 at 80 because the race was not reproduced, F13 at 70 because a WAF may exist), and the deploy checklist sequences operational risk, including rollback after migration. As with E, the ranking itself is by severity.
expl_justification.trade_offs: It compares alternatives throughout. New *Visiveis functions are preferred over optional parameters. HTTP 200 for both foreign and missing tickets avoids an id oracle. mediaResposta stays global, with the product owner left to decide. Wildcards are kept. Timing equalization during migration is rejected as false security. Removing the fallback is set against the outage it causes, and the EXPORT_DIR file's removal is flagged for consumers. The formula prefix is applied to data billing reads, but the cost ('+55 11 ...' gains an apostrophe) and the one-line reversal are stated. It does not weigh declining it outright, as I and K did.
